C-ADAPTIVE-ACTION-CENTER.Summary: Deliver a stable adaptive action center that launches existing Kafedra Planner workflows and routes any supported uploaded document to the exact materialized domain object without duplicating parsers or forms.
C-ADAPTIVE-ACTION-CENTER.Problem: The global create control previously opened only a calendar form while plans, documents, directives, meetings, templates, periodic work and science flows had separate entry points. A user who already selected a file also had to know its destination in advance, despite the deterministic document worker being able to classify and materialize supported domain objects.

Goals.Goal: Replace the global create entry point with one keyboard-accessible center containing a stable catalog, exactly three fixed recommendation slots and a universal document drop zone.
Rank recommendations deterministically by explicit context, domain-derived context, calendar period, personal frequency and static fallback without changing layout or automatically launching actions.
Preserve the existing feature launchers and document processing pipeline; the center is an orchestration layer, not a second parser, form set or source of truth.
After upload, follow the exact returned documentId and open the plan, meeting, directive or science object created or linked by that document's extraction run.

Make protocol materialization safely reuse one unambiguous meeting, add only non-conflicting missing facts and agenda items, retain evidence, and convert conflicts into review items instead of overwriting durable data.
Cover desktop, mobile, keyboard, focus, reduced motion, degraded preference behavior, partial success and idempotent retries with automated tests.

Constraints.Constraint: The application remains fully operational offline on Debian and Astra Linux without Docker, CDN, mandatory Internet, cloud services or mandatory LLM.
Original blobs, SHA-256, document versions, structural locators and extraction evidence remain immutable.
Action recommendations are rank-only. Explicit current context and domain-derived facts are stronger than learned frequency, and programmatic routing never records a learned user choice.
The center must not duplicate domain forms, parsers, materializers, persisted entities or projections.
Unknown, failed or ambiguous documents remain saved and accessible; one bad row or fragment must not block safely recognized data.
Protocol merge may use the same source version or one unambiguous exact normalized protocol number plus exact date; conflicting durable facts are never overwritten silently.
No existing SQL migration is edited, renamed or removed. This change does not require a new migration or VERSION change.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Replace existing calendar, plans, meetings, directives, templates, review, science or report editors.
Introduce semantic embeddings, a remote classifier, mandatory llama.cpp or an autonomous destructive agent.
Redesign every application screen or reorder permanent navigation from usage statistics.
Automatically resolve ambiguous people, dates, permissions, deletion, completion or other never-learn actions.
Change the SQLite schema, package version, release artifacts or installer contract.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: The top-bar control is labelled + Добавить and the same center opens from Ctrl/Cmd+N and the plus control of a concrete calendar day.
The center always exposes five fixed groups, exactly three recommendation slots, deterministic text search and a universal supported-file drop zone without geometry changes caused by statistics.
Clicking a concrete calendar day preserves that exact domain-derived date when the user chooses a task or event, regardless of learned frequency.
The action registry is the single catalog and learned frequency may only reorder registered available actions; the server rejects unknown action IDs.
The preference/context layer may fail without blocking the static catalog, existing launchers or document upload.
An uploaded file is persisted through the normal immutable document intake before classification and is never uploaded a second time merely to continue a domain flow.

The client observes the exact documentId returned by upload and opens the materialized plan, meeting, directive or science ID stored in that document's extraction result, never the last object in a section.
A processed plan opens its actual plan and source rows; ambiguous rows remain editable and do not block other rows.

A protocol opens the exact created or unambiguously matched meeting; safe missing agenda facts are added idempotently, while conflicting fields create review items and preserve existing values and evidence.
Repeated protocol materialization creates no duplicate meeting, agenda item, decision, calendar item, open review item or identical search fragment.
An unknown, failed or ambiguous document remains accessible as a generic document or review target with an understandable status.
The dialog supports keyboard focus containment, Escape close, focus restoration, desktop and mobile completion, and a static understandable prefers-reduced-motion fallback.

Unit, integration and Playwright desktop/mobile tests cover precedence, allowlist validation, exact object routing, multi-question protocols, conflict preservation, partial/degraded behavior and reduced motion.
npm run check, npm test, smoke, backup self-test, full browser tests, GRACE target/final, project CI and post-merge CI complete successfully on their exact heads.
The change is delivered through an ordinary PR, exact-head squash merge, successful post-merge CI and a separate archive-only PR placing this change in terminal applied state.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Exact-head tests and CI demonstrate stable action geometry, context precedence, immutable upload, exact materialized-object routing, safe protocol merge, idempotency, desktop/mobile accessibility and unchanged offline/recovery compatibility.

Assumptions.Assumption: The governed implementation branch was created from exact main commit adee48d5df671aeba9dd5c5f36f607747705430f.
Issue 200 is the human-visible work item and PR 204 is the governed implementation pull request.
The current UI remains rooted in public and the existing feature modules continue to expose their established launch controls and window adapters.
The existing ui_choice_preferences table is sufficient for action.center.action and therefore no migration is needed.
